authorial_core.baseline_prompt_en: A photographic LitRPG scene in which RPG rules are visible inside the lived fantasy world. A fantasy artisan and customer share a cold glassworking counter, where an item appraisal changes a purchase decision. The fictional woman maker has a face and short dark bob with fine fringe guided by the supplied reference portrait. Her identity, occupation and circumstances belong to this fictional scene. At the shutter she has just finished a blue glass lantern vial for a marsh surveyor before his morning departure. What looked like a trapped white flaw proves useful in dense marsh fog. She steadies the cooled vial by its broad foot with the thumb and index finger of her left hand, her wrist extending naturally from the forearm resting along the stone counter. Her other hand rests beside a copper glassworking rod. The customer stands across the right end of the counter, shoulders and both forearms visible; his right fingers set three silver coins onto a small leather payment square while his gaze follows the vial and its appraisal. A folded marsh map protrudes from his satchel. Her quiet confidence and the customer's slightly raised brows make the small revaluation readable. The vial occupies a clear central space between their hands. A restrained translucent appraisal card floats directly above it; its readable item statistics point to that same physical item by a thin line ending at the white seed inside the glass. The large spare text reads "LANTERN VIAL", "UNCOMMON", "MIST SIGHT +12", "18 SILVER". A smaller separate badge beside the maker's apron reads "GLASSCRAFT Lv.7" and "XP 84/100", visibly assigning the craft progression to her. The glass transmits cool daylight while its trapped seed gives a restrained amber glimmer. A cutting collar, glass shears and a cooling rack place the transaction in a working craft shop; the furnace opening is a low warm patch in the rear. Use a landscape medium view from the near corner of the counter, a normal lens and sufficient depth to resolve both faces, hands, the vial and full appraisal card together. The glassblower's open-neck ivory linen work blouse and weathered brown waist apron catch soft window light; subtle skin texture, luminous eyes and an unforced expression carry her personal appeal. Warm furnace color recedes behind the cool precise glass. Grounded photographic material, an intimate but practical working distance, and a clear hierarchy from maker's expression to the vial to the buyer's payment.
